arxiv-2104-09610.title: Geometric methods for efficient planar swimming of copepod nauplii Thanks: M.C. is partially supported by the Simons Foundation grant number 359510.
arxiv-2104-09610.creator: Jonas Balisacan, Monique Chyba, Corey Shanbrom, George Wilkens
arxiv-2104-09610.description: Abstract . Copepod nauplii are larval crustaceans with important ecological functions. Due to their small size, they experience an environment of low Reynolds number within their aquatic habitat. Here we provide a mathematical model of a swimming copepod nauplius with two legs moving in a plane.

arxiv-2106-08400.title: Traveling chimera patterns in two-dimensional neuronal network
arxiv-2106-08400.creator: Gaël R. Simo 1, Patrick Louodop 1, Dibakar Ghosh 2, Thierry Njougou 1, Robert Tchitnga, 1,3, Hilda A. Cerdeira 4,5
arxiv-2106-08400.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Gaël R. Simo 1, Patrick Louodop 1, Dibakar Ghosh 2, Thierry Njougou 1, Robert Tchitnga, 1,3, Hilda A. Cerdeira 4,5. We study the emergence of the traveling chimera state in a two-dimensional network of Hindmarsh-Rose burst neurons with the mutual presence of local and non-local couplings. We show that in the unique presence of the non-local chemical coupling modeled by a nonlinear function, the traveling chimera phenomenon occurs with a displacement in both directions of the plane of the grid.

arxiv-2111-13075.title: Predicting the success of Gradient Descent for a particular Dataset-Architecture-Initialization (DAI)
arxiv-2111-13075.creator: Umangi Jain, Harish G. Ramaswamy
arxiv-2111-13075.description: Abstract Despite their massive success, training successful deep neural networks still largely relies on experimentally choosing an architecture, hyper-parameters, initialization, and training mechanism. In this work, we focus on determining the success of standard gradient descent method for training deep neural networks on a specified dataset, architecture, and initialization (DAI) combination.

arxiv-2211-00605.creator: Marco Roveri, Franc Ivankovic, Luigi Palopoli, Daniele Fontanelli
arxiv-2211-00605.description: Abstract There is a growing interest in modeling and analyzing the spread of diseases like the SARS-CoV-2 infection using stochastic models. These models are typically analyzed quantitatively and are not often subject to validation using formal verification approaches, nor leverage policy syntheses and analysis techniques developed in formal verification.

arxiv-2212-01494.title: Caustic-like Structures in UHECR Flux after Propagation in Turbulent Intergalactic Magnetic Fields
arxiv-2212-01494.creator: K. Dolgikh 1,2 , A. Korochkin 3,2 , G. Rubtsov 1,2 , D. Semikoz 4 , and I. Tkachev 1,2
arxiv-2212-01494.description: Abstract UHECR propagation in a turbulent intergalactic magnetic field in the small-angle scattering regime is well understood for propagation distances much larger than the field coherence scale. The diffusion theory doesn’t work and unexpected effects may appear for propagation over smaller distances, from a few and up to 10-20 coherence scales.

arxiv-2301-06528.description: Abstract I Introduction Brain stroke is a devastating medical condition, that affects world population and is the main cause of disabilities worldwide [ 1 ] . Disabilities related to stroke can affect motor pathways, and may lead to several motor function disorders.

arxiv-2304-14449.title: Probing localization properties of many-body Hamiltonians via an imaginary vector potential
arxiv-2304-14449.creator: Liam O’Brien, Gil Refael
arxiv-2304-14449.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Liam O’Brien, Gil Refael. Identifying and measuring the “localization length” in many-body systems in the vicinity of a many-body localization transition is difficult. Following Hatano and Nelson, a recent work [S. B 103 , 064201 (2021)] introduced an “imaginary vector potential” to a disordered ring of interacting fermions, in order to define a many-body localization length (corresponding, in the non-interacting case, to the end-to-end Green’s function of the hermitian system).

arxiv-2409-17734.title: Role of coherence in many-body Quantum Reservoir Computing
arxiv-2409-17734.creator: Ana Palacios, Rodrigo Martínez-Peña, Miguel C. Soriano, Gian Luca Giorgi, Roberta Zambrini
arxiv-2409-17734.description: Abstract Quantum Reservoir Computing (QRC) offers potential advantages over classical reservoir computing, including inherent processing of quantum inputs and a vast Hilbert space for state exploration. Yet, the relation between the performance of reservoirs based on complex and many-body quantum systems and non-classical state features is not established.

arxiv-2502-07805.title: Simultaneous kinetic profile and magnetic equilibrium inference with Bayesian integrated data analysis in preparation for ITER
arxiv-2502-07805.creator: S. S. Denk, T. B. Amara, T. Odstrčil, L. Stagner, C. Akcay, T. Slendebroek, S. P. Smith, M. A. Van Zeeland, T. Akiyama, R. Nazikian

Accurate plasma state reconstruction will be crucial for the success of ITER and future fusion plants, but the harsh conditions of a burning plasma will make diagnostic operation more challenging than in current machines.

arxiv-2506-07557.title: SELT: Self-Evaluation Tree Search for LLMs with Task Decomposition
arxiv-2506-07557.creator: Mengsong Wu, Di Zhang, Yuqiang Li, Dongzhan Zhou, Wenliang Chen
arxiv-2506-07557.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mengsong Wu, Di Zhang, Yuqiang Li, Dongzhan Zhou, Wenliang Chen. While Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success in a wide range of applications, their performance often degrades in complex reasoning tasks. In this work, we introduce SELT ( S elf- E valuation L LM T ree Search), a novel framework that leverages a modified Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to enhance LLM reasoning without relying on external reward models.

arxiv-2507-06032.title: Learning-Augmented Online Covering Problems
arxiv-2507-06032.creator: Afrouz Jabal Ameli, Laura Sanità, Moritz Venzin
arxiv-2507-06032.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Afrouz Jabal Ameli, Laura Sanità, Moritz Venzin. We give a very general and simple framework to incorporate predictions on requests for online covering problems in a rigorous and black-box manner. Our framework turns any online algorithm with competitive ratio ρ ⁡ ( k , ⋅ ) \rho(k,\cdot) depending on k k , the number of arriving requests, into an algorithm with competitive ratio of ρ ⁡ ( η , ⋅ ) \rho(\eta,\cdot) , where η \eta is the prediction error.

pmc-10535273.description: While an important part of the world’s population is vaccinated against SARS-CoV-2, new variants continue to emerge. We observe that even after a fifth dose of the mRNA bivalent vaccine, most vaccinated individuals have antibodies that poorly neutralize several Omicron subvariants, including BQ.1.1, XBB, XBB.1.5, FD.1.1, and CH.1.1.

pmc-10662746.title: A zero-agnostic model for copy number evolution in cancer
pmc-10662746.creator: Henri Schmidt, Palash Sashittal, Benjamin J. Raphael, Zhaolei Zhang, Philipp M Altrock, Zhaolei Zhang, Philipp M Altrock, Zhaolei Zhang, Philipp M Altrock
pmc-10662746.description: MotivationNew low-coverage single-cell DNA sequencing technologies enable the measurement of copy number profiles from thousands of individual cells within tumors. From this data, one can infer the evolutionary history of the tumor by modeling transformations of the genome via copy number aberrations. Copy number aberrations alter multiple adjacent genomic loci, violating the standard phylogenetic assumption that loci evolve independently.

pmc-11317461.title: Editorial: Liquid biopsy in oncology: opportunity and challenges
pmc-11317461.creator: Ashok Kumar, Rajesh Singh, Neha Arya, Smiths Lueong, Aklank Jain
pmc-11317461.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ssessing recurrence risk. Typically, cancer diagnosis for solid tumors relies on invasive tumor biopsy, which is associated with limited access to deep-seated tumors, and intra-tumor heterogeneity. Towards this, liquid biopsy can overcome these limitations and provide a comprehensive and accurate reflection of the tumor’s molecular landscape and find application in cancer screening, classification, determining treatment options, monitoring treatment responses, and detecting minimal residual disease post-surgery.

pmc-11655635.title: MiR-378 exaggerates angiogenesis and bone erosion in collagen-induced arthritis mice by regulating endoplasmic reticulum stress
pmc-11655635.creator: Zhengmeng Yang, Nan Hou, Wenxiang Cheng, Xuan Lu, Ming Wang, Shanshan Bai, Yuejun Lin, Yaofeng Wang, Sien Lin, Peng Zhang, Micky D Tortorella, Lu Feng, Gang Li
pmc-11655635.description: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disorder marked by pain, inflammation, and discomfort in the synovial joints. It is critical to understand the pathological mechanisms of RA progression. MicroRNA-378 (miR-378) is highly expressed in the synovium of RA patients and positively correlated with disease severity, but its function and underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood.

pmc-12427305.description: Simple SummaryBreast cancer is the most common cancer among women worldwide, and current screening methods are primarily based on imaging.
